newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Guangzhou Inv mulls stakes in five hotels.
newsitem.headline: Guangzhou Inv mulls stakes in five hotels.

text.p: Guangzhou Investment Co Ltd is in discussions to buy stakes in five hotels in China and Hong Kong from its direct parent, Yue Xiu Enterprises (Holdings) Ltd, the company's deputy general manager said on Monday.
"We (Guangzhou Investment) are in discussions to buy into five hotels, of which four are in China and one in Hong Kong," Liang Ningguang told a news conference.

"We initially planned to buy control in three of the five hotels, including the one in Hong Kong, but details have yet to be finalised," Liang said. South China Hotel in North Point was their purchasing target in Hong Kong, he added.
Liang declined to comment on the investment involved.

Guangzhou Investment, an investment arm of the Guangzhou Municipal government in China, raised about HK$2.2 billion from the recent spin off of GZI Transport Ltd and placement of new shares, the company said in a statement.
"The conversion of outstanding convertible bonds further reduced its gearing ratio substantially. The group is now in a strong position to fund new investments," it said.
It would also consider acquisiton of investment properties in prime locations with secured tenancy in Guangzhou.
The company aimed to build up a bigger recurrent income base in 1997 by further expanding the toll road business and investing into Guangzhou property projects with stable income.

"The group will expand toll road business primarily in Guangdong and selectively in other regions of the PRC (People's Republic of China," it said in a statement. Guangzhou Investment said it will also focus on Guangzhou's residential sector to take advantage of the strong demand from local buyers for midddle-market residential properties and government low-price housing schemes with guaranteed returns.
